item.title: Suicide is up among Black Americans. We need to talk about it.
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin hosted a panel conversation about mental health and suicide in the Black community, exploring a difficult subject in deeply personal conversations.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Michel Martin hosted a panel conversation about mental health and suicide in the Black community, exploring a difficult subject in deeply personal conversations.

item.title: New U.S. indictment charges former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro with torture
item.description: U.S. authorities added new torture charges to their case against former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, ramping up pressure on the ousted authoritarian leader already fighting drug trafficking allegations.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: 4 people on NASA's Crew-12 mission return to Earth after 8 months in space
item.description: Four people — two NASA astronauts, one from the European Space Agency and a Russian cosmonaut — spent nearly eight months at the space station, conducting spacewalks, science experiments and research.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: White House correspondent April Ryan reflects on reporting while under attack
item.description: Ryan has spent decades pressing presidents for answers. She talks about access, power, race and how asking questions put her in President Trump's crosshairs. Her new book is Notes on a Blacklash.
item.content:encoded: Ryan has spent decades pressing presidents for answers. She talks about access, power, race and how asking questions put her in President Trump's crosshairs. Her new book is Notes on a Blacklash.

item.title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute
item.description: The South Korean announcement on Thursday came days after its President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation.

item.title: South Korea test-flies its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon
item.description: The test follows North Korea's recent hypersonic missile test. Tensions between the Koreas have increased after land mine explosions injured three South Korean soldiers near the border. North Korea denies responsibility.

item.title: Isaias intensifies to hurricane. And, judge orders Pike execution evidence preserved
item.description: People in the Gulf are preparing for bad weather this weekend after Isaias intensified into a hurricane. And, a judge has ordered Christa Pike's failed execution evidence be preserved.

item.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
item.description: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.
